shows.title: Willem de Kooning Drawing
shows.why: Bringing together more than 200 artworks from around the world, this major exhibition is the first to examine Abstract Expressionist Willem de Kooning’s expansive drawing practice across his seven-decade career.

shows.title: Beyond Form: Abstraction at Midcentury
shows.why: Featuring 65 artists from more than 23 countries, this exhibition explores how abstraction emerged as a powerful visual language between 1940 and 1970, a period of global upheaval and transformation.

shows.title: Self, Made: Fourteen Modern Artists from the Richard and Ellen Sandor Family Collection
shows.why: This exhibition tells stories of self-invention in photography, drawing, and sculpture, most of them from artists working beyond the gallery and museum system that typically validates creative work.

shows.title: The Floating World Emerges: Japanese Prints from the Clarence Buckingham Collection
shows.why: This presentation brings together about 40 "pictures of the floating world" prints, many given to the museum by a major collector and an early supporter of the Art Institute, Clarence Buckingham.

shows.title: Edgar Calel: Corn Mountain of Life (Ixim Juyu K’aslem)
shows.why: Guatemala-born artist Edgar Calel brings elements of his Maya-Kaqchikel family and community to Chicago with an installation that merges practical needs and ceremonial meanings.

shows.title: Nora Turato: I hear you, I hear you.
